questions.title: Section A – Multiple Choice, Terms, Matching, Nervous System Diagram & Ear Diagrams

subQuestions.questionText:
Diabetes mellitus is caused by an …

A oversecretion of glucagon.
B undersecretion of glucagon.
C oversecretion of insulin.
D undersecretion of insulin.

Receptors that are stimulated by the low water levels in the blood are located in the …

A renal tubules.
B hypothalamus.
C pituitary gland.
D carotid artery.

The myelin sheath on a nerve cell …

A provides electrical insulation.
B transports impulses towards the cell body.
C receives impulses from the axon.
D converts stimuli into impulses.

options.B: transports impulses towards the cell body.

subQuestions.questionText:
The structure where sperms are temporarily stored is the …

A testis.
B epididymis.
C vas deferens.
D penis.

Which ONE of the following is a function of the amniotic fluid?

A Provides nutrition to the foetus
B Protects the foetus against mechanical injury
C Supplies oxygen to the foetus
D Removes the metabolic waste from the foetus

options.B: Protects the foetus against mechanical injury
options.D: Removes the metabolic waste from the foetus

subQuestions.questionText:
Based on the diagram of the brain (parts labelled 1–4): Which ONE of the following represents the corpus callosum?

A 1
B 2
C 3
D 4

Based on the diagram of the brain: Which ONE of the following is the function of part 3 (cerebellum)?

A Controls voluntary movements
B Controls involuntary actions
C Coordinates voluntary movements
D Controls all sensations

The placenta is formed by the …

A amniotic fluid and amnion.
B chorionic villi and endometrium.
C amnion and endometrium.
D amniotic fluid and chorionic villi.

An oversecretion of the hormone produced by the thyroid gland may result in a person …

A gaining weight, because of an increased metabolic rate.
B gaining weight, because of a decreased metabolic rate.
C losing weight, because of an increased metabolic rate.
D losing weight, because of a decreased metabolic rate.

options.A: gaining weight, because of an increased metabolic rate.
options.B: gaining weight, because of a decreased metabolic rate.
options.C: losing weight, because of an increased metabolic rate.
options.D: losing weight, because of a decreased metabolic rate.

subQuestions.questionText:
A table shows average testosterone levels: Group I (0–10 years) <5 n/M; Group II (11–15 years) 15 n/M; Group III (16–20 years) 19 n/M. Which ONE is an explanation for the difference in testosterone levels?

A Group I than Group III due to the start of puberty.
B Group II than Group I due to the start of puberty.
C Group III than Group I because it is needed to inhibit the growth of long bones.
D Group I than Group II because it is needed to inhibit the growth of long bones.

options.A: Group I than Group III due to the start of puberty.
options.B: Group II than Group I due to the start of puberty.
options.C: Group III than Group I because it is needed to inhibit the growth of long bones.
options.D: Group I than Group II because it is needed to inhibit the growth of long bones.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for: The process of maintaining a constant internal environment in the human body.
Give the correct biological term for: The organelles found in large quantities in the neck region of a sperm cell.
Give the correct biological term for: The disease characterised by the degeneration of brain tissue, leading to memory loss.
Give the correct biological term for: The layer in the eye that is richly supplied with blood vessels.
Give the correct biological term for: The type of development in birds in which the young is born fully developed and able to move and feed itself.
Give the correct biological term for: Groups of cells in the pancreas that secrete insulin and glucagon.
Give the correct biological term for: The structure in the sperm that contains enzymes to dissolve the outer layer of the ovum.
Give the correct biological term for: A blood vessel that transports carbon dioxide from the foetus to the placenta.

Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B, or NONE.

Description: An extra-embryonic membrane found in the amniotic egg.
A: Chorion
B: Allantois

Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B, or NONE.

Description: A structure in the ear that absorbs excess pressure waves from the cochlea.
A: Pinna
B: Auditory canal

Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B, or NONE.

Description: A structure that transports semen out of the body.
A: Scrotum
B: Urethra

subQuestions.label: 1.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The flow diagram represents the components of the nervous system (Nervous System → Central nervous system + A; Central nervous system → Brain + B; A → Cranial nerves + C; C → D; D → Sympathetic nervous system + E). Identify the component represented by A.

subQuestions.label: 1.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the component of the nervous system represented by D in the flow diagram.
Name the type of nerves found at C (branching from the peripheral nervous system alongside cranial nerves).
Give the LETTER and NAME of the component that slows down the heart rate when an emergency situation has passed.
Name the nerve cells that make up nervous tissue.
State TWO ways in which the brain is protected.
subQuestions.memoText: Any two of: Meninges; Cranium / bone tissue; Cerebrospinal fluid. (Mark first TWO only.)

subQuestions.questionText: The diagrams show parts of the middle and inner ear (Diagram 1: parts A–D; Diagram 2: part F). Identify part F.
Give the collective term for bones B in the ear diagram.

subQuestions.label: 1.5.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the LETTER and NAME of the structure that equalises pressure between the outer and middle ear.

subQuestions.label: 1.5.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the LETTER and NAME of the structure that creates pressure waves in the inner ear.

subQuestions.label: 1.5.4(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the receptors that are stimulated by a change in the position of the head.

subQuestions.label: 1.5.4(b)

questions.title: Female Reproduction, BPA & Infertility, Spermatogenesis, Frog Reproduction, Thermoregulation & Hearing Loss

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents the female reproductive system (parts A–D). Identify part B.
Name the process that takes place in part A (fallopian tube) that leads to zygote formation.
Describe the process of fertilisation.
subQuestions.memoText: The nucleus of the sperm fuses with the nucleus of the ovum.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the development of the zygote until implantation occurs.
subQuestions.memoText: Zygote divides by mitosis to form a solid ball of cells called the morula, which develops into a hollow ball of cells called the blastula / blastocyst. (Any 4 points)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO ways in which part D (uterus) is structurally suited for gestation.
subQuestions.memoText: Any two of: It is muscular – to protect the foetus from mechanical injury / to allow for parturition / birth; It is flexible / can expand – to accommodate the growing foetus; It is hollow – to accommodate the growing foetus; The thickened endometrium – allows for implantation / survival of the embryo. (Mark first TWO only; 2 marks each.)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how the secretion of the prostate gland provides protection for the sperm from the conditions in part C (vagina).
subQuestions.memoText: The secretion is alkaline which neutralises the acidic conditions of the vagina.

subQuestions.questionText: BPA interferes with normal FSH secretion. State ONE function of FSH.
subQuestions.memoText: Stimulates the development of ovarian follicles / Initiates puberty. (Mark first ONE only.)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE other hormone in females that is secreted by the pituitary gland during the menstrual cycle.
Explain how an undersecretion of LH (the hormone named in 2.2.2) may lead to infertility.
subQuestions.memoText: LH stimulates ovulation; therefore ovulation will not take place and there will be no ovum to fertilise. (Any 2 points)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why a decrease in the maturation of ovarian follicles may lead to reduced implantation rates.
subQuestions.memoText: A Graafian follicle is not formed; since the Graafian follicle secretes oestrogen, oestrogen levels will be reduced; therefore the endometrium will not develop / thicken; and no implantation can take place. OR: There is no ovum produced / a Graafian follicle is not formed; ovulation does not occur; no fertilisation occurs; a zygote is not formed; and no implantation can take place.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the process of spermatogenesis.
subQuestions.memoText: Under the influence of testosterone, diploid cells / germinal epithelium cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testis undergo meiosis to form haploid sperm. (Any 4 points)

subQuestions.questionText: Male and female frogs release millions of gametes into the water during breeding season. Name the type of fertilisation described.
Explain why millions of gametes are released by frogs.
subQuestions.memoText: To increase the chances of fertilisation since the gametes may be lost / not reach one another due to predation / water currents. OR: To produce more zygotes / offspring since many will be lost because they are preyed on / washed away / dry out.

subQuestions.questionText: State why the reproduction in frogs is an example of ovipary.
subQuestions.memoText: The embryos develop inside an egg, outside the female's body.

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows parts of the skin involved in thermoregulation (A = sweat gland, B = blood vessel). Give TWO reasons why part A is classified as an exocrine gland.
subQuestions.memoText: Any two of: It has a duct; The secretion is released externally / not released into blood; It secretes sweat / it does not secrete a hormone. (Mark first TWO only.)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the role of skin receptors in thermoregulation.
subQuestions.memoText: They receive stimuli from the environment and convert them to nerve impulses.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why structure B (blood vessel) dilates on a hot day.
subQuestions.memoText: More blood flows to the surface of the skin to allow more heat to be lost. OR: More blood flows to the sweat glands to increase the production of sweat.

subQuestions.questionText: Workers exposed to loud noise can destroy hair cells in the organ of Corti. Name the structure in the ear where the organ of Corti is located.
Calculate the percentage increase in the number of factory workers with hearing loss between 2014 (85 000) and 2018 (130 000). Show ALL workings.
Suggest ONE reason for the increase in the number of factory workers with hearing loss caused by exposure to loud noise in this developing country.
subQuestions.memoText: Any one of: More factories were built – increase in supply and demand; More workers were employed; Extended exposure to loud sounds; Lack of precautionary measures. (Mark first ONE only.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why damage to the auditory nerve may result in hearing loss.
subQuestions.memoText: The impulse will not be transmitted to the cerebrum and will not be interpreted.

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a bar graph to represent the data in the table (Year vs Number of factory workers with hearing loss: 2014=85 000; 2015=100 000; 2016=115 000; 2017=120 000; 2018=130 000).
subQuestions.memoText: Mark scheme (6 marks): Type – bar graph drawn (1); Caption of graph includes both variables (1); Correct labels on x-axis and y-axis (1); Correct scale for y-axis, equal width of bars and spaces (1); Plotting – 1–4 coordinates plotted correctly (1), all 5 coordinates plotted correctly (2).

questions.title: Plant Hormones, Geotropism, Aldosterone Investigation, Adrenalin & Human Eye

subQuestions.questionText: The graph shows abscisic acid concentration in a cherry tree during different seasons (March–November). During which month was the abscisic acid concentration the lowest?
Explain the trend of the graph from March to May (abscisic acid concentration increases).
subQuestions.memoText: The concentration of abscisic acid increases to stimulate the abscission / falling of leaves, to prepare the tree for dormancy. Less sunlight / less water / cold conditions therefore decreased photosynthesis / reduced transpiration / lower energy demand / low growth rate. (Any 1 x 2; mark first ONE only.)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ONE reason for the dormancy in cherry trees during the winter months.
subQuestions.memoText: Less sunlight / less water / cold conditions therefore decreased photosynthesis / reduced transpiration / lower energy demand / low growth rate. (Any 1 x 2; mark first ONE only.)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the role of auxins in roots.
subQuestions.memoText: Auxins promote the development of roots; it brings about general root growth causing their downward growth / positive geotropism.

subQuestions.questionText: When a plant is placed horizontally with light from all directions, auxins accumulate on the lower side of both the stem and the roots. Explain the difference in the response of the stem and the roots after a few days.
subQuestions.memoText: In the stem, the auxins stimulate growth on the lower side causing the stem to grow / bend upwards. In the root, the auxins inhibit growth on the lower side causing the root to grow / bend downwards.

subQuestions.questionText: Hyperaldosteronism is caused by oversecretion of aldosterone. Name the gland that secretes aldosterone.

subQuestions.label: 3.3.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Scientists investigated the influence of increased aldosterone levels on blood pressure in 1 688 volunteers. Identify the independent variable.

subQuestions.label: 3.3.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the dependent variable in the aldosterone investigation.
Give TWO reasons why the results of the aldosterone investigation may be considered reliable.
subQuestions.memoText: Any two of: 1 688 volunteers were used; The procedure was done 4 times for each individual. (Mark first TWO only.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO reasons why it was important for the participants to follow the same diet during the investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: All factors should be kept constant / there should be only one independent variable, to ensure the validity of the investigation; Dietary factors / examples can also influence blood pressure. (2 x 2; mark first TWO only.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the participants' blood pressure was measured before the start of the investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: To compare the blood pressure before and after the administration of aldosterone.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the levels of salt in the urine of participants is expected to decrease after being injected with aldosterone.
subQuestions.memoText: The high aldosterone level will increase the permeability of the renal tubules for salt; more salt will be reabsorbed (and therefore less salt will be excreted in urine).

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how the secretion of adrenalin causes increased energy production in an emergency situation.
subQuestions.memoText: Any 8 of: Adrenalin causes glycogen to be converted to glucose which increases the blood glucose level; the breathing muscles are stimulated to increase the rate and depth of breathing; the heart muscle is stimulated to pump faster; there is also an increase in blood pressure, increasing the transport of oxygen and glucose; the rate of cellular respiration is increased.

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents the human eye (parts A–F, including vitreous humour A, retina B, blind spot/optic nerve C, lens D, cornea E, iris F). Identify structure F.
State TWO functions of fluid A (vitreous humour) in the human eye.
subQuestions.memoText: Any two of: Helps to maintain the shape of the eye; plays a role in refraction of light; allows the transmission of light; prevents desiccation of structures in the eye; holds the retina in position; nourishment of the eye; prevents mechanical injury in the eye. (Mark first TWO only.)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the structural difference between area B (fovea / yellow spot) and area C (blind spot) in the human eye.
subQuestions.memoText: Area B contains a high concentration of photoreceptors / cones; area C contains no photoreceptors / no rods and cones.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the visual defect that occurs when the curvature of part E (cornea) is uneven.
Explain how the sight of a person will be affected if cataracts developed in part D (lens).
subQuestions.memoText: Because the lens will become cloudy / opaque; no / less light will enter the eye; causing no sight / weak sight.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the process of accommodation that takes place when an object is less than 6 metres away from the eye.
subQuestions.memoText: Any 6 of: The ciliary muscle contracts; the ciliary body moves closer to the lens; the suspensory ligaments slacken; tension on the lens decreases; the lens becomes more convex / rounded; light rays are refracted more; to focus the light on the retina.
